description: Summer internships in Rep. Angie Craig's office will be held in-person in the Washington, D.C. office. The D.C. internship will run approximately from May 26th, 2026, through Early August, with some room for flexibility. All interns are paid a stipend and provided with the necessary technology for their work. Schedules are flexible to accommodate course schedules and academic programs; however, a minimum availability of 20-25 hours per week is highly preferred. All interns will have the opportunity to work with staff in both the D.C. and district offices over the course of the internship and the program is easily tailored to fit interns' policy interests and career goals. As a result, interns will learn about the legislative process, learn about all the different functions of a congressional office and gain hands-on professional experience while serving the constituents of Minnesota's Second Congressional District.
responsibilities: Work with staff in both the D.C. and district offices over the course of the internship
Learn about the legislative process
Learn about all the different functions of a congressional office
Gain hands-on professional experience while serving the constituents of Minnesota's Second Congressional District
qualifications: Passionate about public service
Confident and effective communicators
Proactive problem-solvers
Possess strong writing skills
Comfortable speaking on the phone and working with the general public
Minimum availability of 20-25 hours per week is highly preferred
how_to_apply: Email a combined PDF of your resume and one-page cover letter to craig.internships@mail.house.gov. Format your email subject line as "FirstName.LastName – DC Office Internship". Include your weekly availability between the hours of 9:00am and 6:00pm in your cover letter and confirm that you will be available for in-person work. Applications must be submitted no later than 9am CT/10am ET on Wednesday, April 1st.
equal_opportunity: Rep. Craig's office is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, age or protected veteran status.

description: The Office of Congressman Gabe Vasquez seeks a part-time, temporary Communications Fellow for the summer (May through August, exact dates flexible). The Communications Fellow is an integral member of the Congressman's office and the communications team. Your role is essential to the office's overall mission of communicating the Congressman and his staff's work on behalf of New Mexicans to his constituents and the press. This is a part-time, temporary position, with 20-25 hours of work per week expected. The schedule is flexible, and a hybrid remote and in-person work arrangement is preferred. Fully remote applicants will also be considered. Fellows will be paid a monthly stipend.

Creating short video clips as needed
Building press lists
qualifications: Excellent writing and graphic design skills
Creativity
Attention to detail
Relevant prior experience
how_to_apply: Send a resume, cover letter, writing sample, and two digital samples with the subject line "NM-02 Spring Communications Fellow" to NM02Press@mail.house.gov by March 25, 2026. No calls or drop-ins, please.
equal_opportunity: The office is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, national origin, disability, military status, age, marital status, or parental status.

description: The Office of Congresswoman Eleanor Holmes Norton provides seasonal internship opportunities to undergraduate and graduate students interested in gaining congressional work experience in her Capitol Hill Office and in her District Office. DC ties are preferred, but not required. Candidates from diverse backgrounds are encouraged to apply. No phone calls or drop-ins please.

how_to_apply: For the Capitol Hill office, email a one-page cover letter, resume, writing sample (2 pages max.), and at least one letter of recommendation as individual attachments to Raya.Kenney@mail.house.gov with subject line: Norton Hill Office Summer 2026 Internship Application - First Name Last Name. description: In the Washington, D.C. office, internships run throughout the year based on the semester calendar. Applicants must be based in Washington, D.C. for the duration of the internship. Spring: Mid-January to mid-May; application window opens in September. Summer: Mid-May to mid-August; application window opens in February. Fall: Early September to mid-December; application window opens in June. Interns in the Washington, D.C. office play an important role in the daily operations of the office and gain firsthand experience in the legislative process. Full-time paid internships run Monday through Friday from 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. when Congress is in session, and 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. when not in session. Part-time internships are scheduled to accommodate students' course schedules, as well as the needs of the office. Part-time interns can expect to receive either pay or academic credit. Internships are intended for current undergraduate students, current graduate students, and recent college graduates.

Other administrative tasks as assigned
